instructions: Bring a large wide pot of water to a boil with 3/4 tsp of the salt.

Meanwhile, trim the roots and the dark green tops off the leeks. Cut each leek into 3 pieces and halve each piece lengthwise. Rinse them well under cold water, spreading the layers to wash out any grit.
Add the leeks to the boiling water and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.

While they cook, finely dice the shallot and chop the leaves from 6 sprigs of parsley. In a bowl, whisk the 1 tbsp vinegar with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt until it dissolves. Stir in the shallot, 1 tbsp Dijon, the parsley and the pepper, then slowly whisk in the olive oil until the dressing thickens.
Lift the leeks out with a slotted spoon and lay them on a clean kitchen towel. Press gently to squeeze out the water. Handle them with care, since they fall apart easily.
Arrange the leeks on a platter and spoon the vinaigrette over them. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve warm, at room temperature or cold. The dressed leeks keep for 2 days in a covered container in the fridge, and are best taken out 20 minutes before eating.
method_notes: Pardon Your French (the lead) simmers leeks until tender, drains them well and spoons over a vinaigrette of shallot, Dijon, parsley, red wine vinegar and a lot of olive oil. Not Quite Nigella cooks the leeks up to 3 days ahead and uses sherry vinegar, balsamic glaze, sugar and crispy shallots; Food.com's version is a plainer oil and vinegar dressing with dry mustard. Neither has 20 ratings, so this is a fallback lead; the egg that many bistro versions add was left out to keep it vegan.
